text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: GPU pool 'infer-prod-eu' showing sustained queue growth + driver Xid/OOM errors — request failure rate rising. Pager routed to on-call.

alex.k: seeing huge backlog on the API side, spike in 5xx for model inference routes. Is this the autoscaler or driver issue?

maria.s: I can see repeated CUDA/Xid errors in node logs, and a couple of nodes flapped earlier. Autoscaler hasn't been adding replicas — hitting the maxReplica limit on the ASG.

kevin: confirmed. Metrics: queued_requests ~ 14k, avg token latency > 1.8s, error_rate ~ 6%. Autoscaler events show "scale at limit".

alex.k: can someone paste the relevant pod/node errors?

maria.s: logs snippet:
```
[2025-11-09T02:11:43Z] GPU0: Xid 31 at 0x7f... driver OOM
[2025-11-09T02:11:44Z] container infer-worker-xx crashloop - OOM killed by kernel
[2025-11-09T02:12:00Z] kubelet: node flapped, network transient
```

kevin: kubectl output: 
```
NAMESPACE   NAME                          READY   STATUS             RESTARTS
inference   infer-worker-abc-0            0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   6
inference   infer-worker-def-1            0/1     OOMKilled          3
```

ops-bot: autoscaler: attempted scale to 40 replicas, current maxReplica=30 — scale blocked.

julia: taking incident lead, on-call until 04:00 UTC. I'll coordinate mitigation. @sre-lead FYI if we need capacity increases.

sre-lead: I'm online. If this is hitting reserved capacity limits we can open emergency capacity, but let's try mitigation first.

julia: immediate plan:
- stop new model heavy requests via routing rule (redirect traffic to lower-cost model)
- temporarily bump autoscaler maxReplica to 50 (if quota allows)
- cordon nodes showing Xid/OOM and drain for investigation
- attempt graceful restart of driver runtime on flapping nodes

alex.k: routing change in place: switched 35% of traffic to small-medium model. Observed immediate drop in queue delta.

kevin: requesting safe bump on autoscaler: current config file:
```yaml
pool: infer-prod-eu
minReplicas: 10
maxReplicas: 30  # requesting override to 50 temporarily
```

ops-bot: request noted. Quota check: region GPU quota available for +20 nodes. Need human approval to modify autoscaler.

maria.s: cordoning node gpu-eu-12 (showing repeated Xid 31) and draining.

maria.s: drain command:
```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-eu-12 && kubectl drain gpu-eu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n inference
```

kevin: driver restart on node gpu-eu-07 executed. Watch logs for Xid recurrence.

alex.k: note — some customers on dedicated accounts may see increased latency; routing change only affects hosted pool. Posting a short customer impact note to status now.

julia: autoscaler bump approved by sre-lead, increasing maxReplica to 50 now.

ops-bot: autoscaler updated: maxReplica -> 50. New desired scaled up to 44.

kevin: new nodes scheduled; watching startup logs. One problematic node (gpu-eu-09) shows NV driver crash during init, marking unhealthy.

maria.s: we've isolated three nodes with repeated driver Xid/OOM (gpu-eu-09, gpu-eu-12, gpu-eu-21). Taking them out of rotation for forensic logs.

alex.k: queue growth rate is slowing — good sign. Error rate down to ~2.1%, queued_requests trending down.

julia: on-call handoff: @kevin will take next 30 mins to stabilize GPU pool, I'll stay for coordination with SRE and customer comms.

kevin: performing rolling restart for infer-worker daemon on the pool to clear potential kernel state:
```bash
kubectl rollout restart deployment/infer-worker -n inference --max-unavailable=10%
```

maria.s: after restarts, seeing fewer Xid entries. nvidia-smi on gpu-eu-11 shows normal state.

sre-lead: are we confident this is driver instability aggregated by the autoscaler pressure rather than a bad container image? Any recent infra rollouts?

maria.s: no infra rollout in last 24h. Kernel OOMs + Xid 31 consistent with memory fragmentation + heavy concurrent sessions. Might be exacerbated by older driver on a subset of nodes. Collecting driver versions.

kevin: mitigation summary so far: routing change for traffic, autoscaler increase, cordon/drain of unhealthy nodes, driver restarts and rolling restarts. Queue down to ~1.5k. Error rate ~0.5%. Latency trending to normal.

alex.k: customer note drafted and posted to status: "Hosted inference in EU region experienced degraded performance due to GPU driver instability causing capacity loss. Some requests were delayed or errored between 02:10–03:05 UTC. We applied mitigations and are monitoring."

julia: tagging for postmortem: need to investigate root cause (driver versions, node hardware differences, autoscaler behavior hitting maxReplica) and add a guard to avoid hitting scale cap silently. Also consider proactive model routing when Xid spikes appear.

kevin: follow-ups: collect nvml logs from cordoned nodes, kernel OOM traces, and autoscaler event logs. Will upload to the incident folder.

maria.s: all cordoned nodes have been re-imaged and rejoined — pool healthy.

ops-bot: autoscaler: scaled down to desired 28 after backlog cleared.

julia: incident status -> mitigated. Will keep thread open for postmortem items. Great work team. :thumbsup:

sre-lead: nice handling. Please include timeline and a customer impact estimate in the postmortem.

kevin: timeline and log bundle uploaded to /incidents/1765432100/artifacts. (link internal)

alex.k: quick notes for PMs: 12% of hosted inference requests in EU were affected at peak, 3% experienced errors.

julia: closing notes: mitigation removed temporary routing after capacity stable. Recommend follow-ups: driver upgrade roll, autoscaler alert for "scale at limit" with pager, and run a soak test on pool after upgrades.

incident-bot: Incident closed (mitigated) by julia at 03:55 UTC. Postmortem assigned to kevin + maria.s.
